description: FlightGear is a free, open-source flight simulator for Windows, macOS and Linux, developed by volunteers around the world. Its about page states that the source code of the entire project is available under the GNU General Public License, and that the goal is a sophisticated and open flight simulator framework for research and academic use, pilot training, engineering work and desktop simulation, which anyone can extend. The project was started because commercial simulators were proprietary and hard to extend, and it is built on contributions from universities, hobbyists and developers. Coverage: worldwide scenery and a range of aircraft models. Format and access: free downloads and source code. Licence and cost: free under the GPL. Caveats: it simulates single aircraft and their flight dynamics, not air traffic networks, and model fidelity varies between aircraft contributed by volunteers. It can serve as the flight engine of human-in-the-loop experiments, digital twin prototypes and emergency procedure studies, such as flights into degraded airports or airspace. It relates to the BlueSky air traffic simulator and BlueSky-Gym in the catalogue, which model traffic, not single-aircraft dynamics.
